NEW DELHI: Rishabh Pant has moved past legendary MS Dhoni to become India’s highest run-scorer as a designated wicketkeeper in away or neutral Tests, adding another major milestone to his growing record book.Pant crossed 2,500 runs in the category during India’s second Test against Sri Lanka in Colombo on Monday, edging past Dhoni’s previous mark of 2,496. Pant has achieved the tally at an average of almost 42, significantly better than Dhoni’s 32.84.Former India wicketkeeper Farokh Engineer is a distant third on the list with 1,209 runs at 32.67, followed by Syed Kirmani with 1,109 at 21.74 and Kiran More with 901 at 29.06.The milestone came a day after Pant had endured an injury scare at the SSC ground. The India wicketkeeper-batter was struck on his left arm by a short delivery from Sri Lanka pacer Lahiru Kumara during the third session on Sunday.Pant attempted to pull the delivery behind square but missed it, taking the full impact on his arm. He was visibly in discomfort and was attended to by the Indian team physiotherapist, who initially applied an ice pack before Pant’s arm was strapped.After making just three runs from 15 balls, Pant walked off the field alongside the physiotherapist in the 58th over.His early departure added to India’s concerns on a day when they were already being tested by Sri Lanka’s bowlers.Despite the blow, Pant returned to the middle on Monday after Sri Lanka claimed India’s sixth wicket through Asitha Fernando, who dismissed debutant Saransh Jain for six.Pant joined Dhruv Jurel with India needing stability and immediately faced another stern examination from the Sri Lankan pacers. Fernando and the other quicks repeatedly tested him with short-pitched deliveries, with Pant taking a couple of blows to the shoulder before the drinks break.The 28-year-old nevertheless showed considerable resilience and continued batting despite the discomfort. Jurel provided valuable support at the other end as the pair put together a crucial partnership to steady India’s innings.
Article Summary: Rishabh Pant becomes India's highest run-scorer as a designated wicketkeeper in away or neutral Tests. Pant crossed 2,500 runs in the category during India’s second Test against Sri Lanka in Colombo. The milestone came a day after Pant had endured an injury scare at the SSC ground.

NEW DELHI: In a leaked audio conversation with pro-Khalistan terrorist Paramjit Singh Pamma, US-based gangster Goldy Brar has admitted to orchestrating the murder of Hardeep Singh Nijjar, a pro-Khalistan terrorist, in Canada in June 2023.Brar said Nijjar, whose killing had triggered a diplomatic crisis between India and Canada, was targeted over his "involvement in drug trafficking and promoting drug abuse". Intelligence sources confirmed the voice in the audio was Brar's.Brar, wanted in India for several killings - including that of singer Sidhu Moosewala - is heard saying Nijjar's promotion of drugs among teens irked him.This admission surfaced alongside the execution of Operation Hardball, a joint US-Canada law enforcement crackdown targeting transnational crime syndicates. The investigation had indicted Brar and Lawrence Bishnoi for orchestrating the killing of ‘HSN’ (short for Nijjar), reframing the high-profile assassination as a gangland hit rather than a state-sponsored killing.“Those who groomed and incited 16-to-17-year-olds to sell drugs... those who blackmailed young people into selling drugs and becoming informants... Nijjar supported and strengthened these individuals so that he could use them when necessary,” Brar is heard telling Pamma.“That’s why me and my team had to kill Nijjar, because these people were using young people to sell drugs. Good or bad, everyone has to face the consequences of their actions,” he added.Brar’s admission, which comes after his and Lawrence’s Op Hardball indictment in Nijjar’s murder, also reflected in Canadian police’s initial probe which hinted at gang rivalry. The probe also noted that a hit on Nijjar had been circulating for several weeks on an encrypted online site used to hire hitmen.Nijjar (45) was shot on June 18, 2023, in the parking lot of Guru Nanak Sikh Gurdwara, in Newton, Surrey. Six men and two vehicles were used in the attack. A CCTV video showed Nijjar’s grey pickup truck and a white sedan driving parallel in the parking lot of the gurdwara, seconds before the shooting started.Nijjar, the head of Khalistan Tiger Force (KTF), was replaced by his confidant Arshdeep Singh alias Arsh Dala. Interestingly, in the latest audio, Brar is also heard claiming the killing of Dala’s close associate, Sukhdool Singh alias Sukha Duneke, who was murdered in Winnipeg area in Sept 2023.

Article Title: Ex-IAF vice-chief Kapoor says India’s 4.5-gen Tejas may not have relevance in 2030s, country must partner with global consortiums like FCAS or GCAP for 6th-gen programme
Article Text:
Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) did not totally rule out the role of Tejas Mk2 in future

NEW DELHI: Less than two months after retirement as the IAF's vice chief, Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor (Retd) has slammed the delay in the delivery of Tejas (LCA) fighter jet by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited to the air force, saying, “why must it be that a machine that was promised to us so many years back with a certain set of capabilities continues to be denied to us on one pretext or the other”.In an interview to NDTV, the IAF veteran said, “Why must we be hamstrung because someone somewhere has not been able to keep their promises?”The delivery of the indigenous LCA Tejas Mk1A jets by HAL to the IAF has faced multi-year delays, primarily caused by late supplies of F404-IN20 engines by American GE company, complex mission software validation, and stringent operational requirements set by the IAF.When asked if advanced Tejas Mk-2 may be operationally relevant when it starts entering service in big numbers in mid 2030s at a time when China is already raising its fleet of its 5th-generation fighter jet, the former vice-chief said, “No, operationally, definitely no.”With China on its way to deploying 500 5th-generation J-20 fighters by 2030, India is still struggling to get the delivery of the first squadron by 4.5-generation Tejas Mk1A. Though the IAF had placed orders for a total of 180 Tejas Mk1A fighter jets long ago, HAL hopes to deliver the first 18-25 Tejas Mk1A only by March 2027.Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) did not totally rule out the role of Tejas Mk2 in future when he said, “You can have a certain number of those 5th generation and 6th generation fighters, but given the size of the country, you won't be able to deploy them everywhere.So those gaps which continue to remain to be filled will have to be filled by this class of aircraft.” “I want Tejas Mk-2 to come, I want India’s 5th-gen AMCA to come. But they must come at a much faster speed,” he said.When asked about Russia’s 5th-gen fighter jet Su-57, the former vice-chief said when the Russian fighter is compared to western jets like American F-35, western jets have an edge over the Su-57 as they have better avionics and stealth.Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) suggested that India should partner with an European consortium working on state-of-the-art sixth generation platforms. “There are other things that are happening — why not join FCAS (Future Combat Air System is the European programme for 6th generation jet under development by French Dassault Aviation, Airbus and Indra Sistemas) Why not GCAP (Global Combat Air Programme is a multinational initiative led by Italy, Japan, and UK to jointly develop a sixth-generation jet).“'You are probably going with a consortium which has got a good record of delivery, of development. Why go through this Gen 4, Gen 4.5 steps when you know the next best thing is already being thought of and why not just join up there?,” the IAF veteran said.His comments underline the difficult choices facing India’s air power planners: meeting immediate squadron requirements while ensuring that indigenous programmes do not fall behind the rapid evolution of military aviation technology.
Article Summary: Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor (Retd) has slammed the delay in the delivery of Tejas (LCA) fighter jet by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited to the air force. “Why must it be that a machine that was promised to us so many years back with a certain set of capabilities continues to be denied to us on one pretext or the other” he said.

Article Title: India was wary of Trump’s ‘unpredictable behaviour’, chose no joint presser with PM Modi: Report

NEW DELHI: India adopted a cautious approach and opted against holding a joint media interaction after Prime Minister Narendra Modi's meeting with US President Donald Trump in France in June amid concerns over the US president's "unpredictable behaviour", government sources told news agency PTI on Monday.The sources said that foreign delegations meeting Trump are often "wary about his unpredictable behaviour as may be seen from his interactions with the presidents of South Africa and Ukraine". "Thus, the cautious approach by India," one of them said, according to PTI.PM Modi and Trump held bilateral talks on June 17 at Evian-les-Bains on the sidelines of the G7 summit. The meeting was seen as an effort to stabilise ties between India and the US after relations had come under strain over the preceding year.The clarification came after US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor said that New Delhi had informed the American side ahead of the meeting that it preferred not to have questions from the media.Gor, speaking at the Economic Times World Leaders Forum on Sunday, had said India wanted media access without a full-fledged press conference. He recalled discussing the matter with Trump before the meeting."We were behind the scenes, behind the stage, and at one point it was just the president and I, and he asked me, he goes, ‘What the Indians are going to raise?’ We went over some topics," Gor said."And he (Trump) said, ‘Do they have any asks?’ And the MEA had one ask. He said, and it was, ‘Let’s bring in the media, but let’s not do a full press conference,’" the ambassador added.Gor said he conveyed the preference to Trump. "I told the president, I said, the Indians prefer no questions. He said, 'Sure, no problem'," he recalled.During the meeting on June 17, Trump also praised PM Modi, saying India would continue to play a major role globally as long as he remained in office. Asked about India's role in West Asia, Trump said: “Yes, I do. I think India plays a big role in everything. As long as he (PM Narendra Modi) is the leader, India is going to play a big role.”Trump also praised PM Modi personally, saying: "So you look at this man. I'll give you a lesson. He's the most beautiful-looking man. He looks so nice. He's like an angel. But actually, he's tough, he's a killer. He's as tough as they come. But he looks so good. So he gets you by surprise," the POTUS said.He added that the US would help India if it came under attack: "If they (India) are attacked and he's (PM Modi) the leader, we would be there to help," Trump said.
Article Summary: PM Modi and Trump held bilateral talks on June 17 at Evian-les-Bains on the sidelines of the G7 summit. Meeting seen as an effort to stabilise ties between India and the US after relations had come under strain over the preceding year. Foreign delegations meeting Trump are often "wary about his unpredictable behaviour"

Article Title: Leg-length gap forces para table tennis champion to halve training
Article Text:
The Moradabad athlete has won 27 national and 10 international medals and recently clinched gold at the 1st UTT Para National Ranking Table Tennis Championship 2026-27 in Indore.

NEW DELHI: A three-inch difference in his leg lengths, persistent back pain and other physical problems have forced 29-year-old Kunal Arora to cut his table tennis training by more than half. Yet, the thalassemia major patient and international para table tennis player is set to leave for Finland on August 26 with the Indian team, even as doctors have advised him to get a prosthetic extension to improve his alignment and mobility.The Moradabad athlete has won 27 national and 10 international medals and recently clinched gold at the 1st UTT Para National Ranking Table Tennis Championship 2026-27 in Indore.Arora will also be felicitated on Sunday by the Thalassemia Patients Advocacy Group (TPAG), in collaboration with Thalassemics India, at an event in New Delhi honouring thalassemia patients for their achievements and resilience.Diagnosed with thalassemia major at birth, Arora said severe iron overload led to two major leg surgeries in 2010. The difference developed gradually as he grew after the surgeries, leaving his left leg around three to four inches shorter than the right.A July 22 prescription records a three-inch left-side limb-length discrepancy and recommends an extension prosthesis with an Axion carbon-fibre foot and laminated socket.Arora said the imbalance has caused spinal curvature, persistent back pain and mobility problems, with doctors recommending the device to improve alignment and daily mobility. He said it would also help during training, though it is unclear if he can wear it in competitions. The prosthesis is estimated to cost Rs 2,66,910 including GST, which his family cannot afford.“My father is a small businessman and my mother is a homemaker. I completed my graduation from Delhi University in 2021 and I am continuing with table tennis. I also help my father with his business whenever he needs me,” Kunal told TOI.The physical problems have cut his training from 7-8 hours in two sessions to about 2.5-3.5 hours in one session. “The difference in my leg length causes pain and affects my daily activities as well as my training. I am now hoping for support to get the prosthetic extension, which costs around Rs 2.7 lakh.I want to continue playing for India and need this support to manage my mobility and training,” he said.Arora has represented India internationally since 2014 and is seeking sponsorship for international tournaments, which he says would help him compete more frequently and work towards the Commonwealth Games, Asian Games and Paralympic Games. For now, he is managing without the prosthesis and plans to give his measurements in the first or second week of September. The device is expected to take about a month to prepare.“Life gave me thalassemia major, but also a choice: to be defined by my diagnosis or my determination. I chose the paddle,” Arora said.
Article Summary: The Moradabad athlete has won 27 national and 10 international medals. Doctors have advised him to get a prosthetic extension to improve his alignment and mobility. The prosthesis is estimated to cost Rs 2,66,910 including GST, which his family cannot afford.

Article Title: Parliament monsoon session yet to be prorogued, BJP, Congress face off over women’s bill

NEW DELHI: BJP on Sunday sought to play back to Rahul Gandhi his pitch for women’s empowerment, by questioning his strident opposition to govt’s push for an early implementation of quota for them in Lok Sabha and assemblies.“He does not want to give rights to women. His words don’t match his actions,” Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis said.BJP’s framing its attack on Rahul around the women’s quota coupled with the fact that monsoon session is yet to be prorogued gave another indication of the possibility of govt summoning the two Houses at short notice to take up its Constitution amendment bill for implementation of quota from 2029 with a nearly 50% rise in Lok Sabha seats.“What explains the abnormal delay now? Is the Union home minister still in search of his super-tainted 2/3rd majority to get the constitutional amendment bill on delimitation passed in a special session,” Congress’s Jairam Ramesh asked.Congress, too, was mindful of the possibility of a short upcoming session and claimed that BJP is still searching for “super tainted” majority in Lok Sabha, in what was a swipe at govt’s alleged attempts to split opposition parties to reach the two-thirds majority in the House needed for the bill’s passage.Ramesh said the gap between Parliament’s adjournment and its prorogation is generally two to four days. But the monsoon session, which ended on Aug 13, has not been prorogued yet.When a session is prorogued, govt has to go through the protocol for calling a new session that conventionally requires a gap of 15 to 20 days.Stepping up BJP’s attack on Rahul Gandhi, Fadnavis said he spoke about women’s empowerment from a public platform but has opposed the most revolutionary step to give women their due.BJP’s Smriti Irani said Rahul should positively respond to PM Modi’s appeal to political parties to support the implementation of women’s quota. On the Vande Mataram row, she said Congress should allow rendition of the song’s full version.While speculation has swirled over the revival of the bill to amend women’s quota law, which was defeated in April, govt has officially remained non-committal over any such move except acknowledging that it had sought Rahul’s view. The LoP in Lok Sabha reiterated his stand against it. Congress and its allies have said Lok Sabha’s strength should be frozen at its existing number and the quota should be executed within it.

Article Title: Many poor in queue, can't allow 'luxury litigation' by rich: SC
Article Text:
SC slams ‘luxury litigation’, says 11-year legal battle delayed genuine cases; imposes Rs 5 lakh cost each

NEW DELHI: At a time when poor litigants have to wait in line for years to get their plea heard, Supreme Court Friday disapproved the practice of influential people indulging in "luxury litigation", resulting in hearing of genuine cases getting delayed. It imposed a cost of Rs 5 lakh each on warring litigants for not approaching the court with "clean hands".A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta rejected the plea of actress Rehana Khan and her lawyer Rizwan Siddique who have been fighting legal battles for past 11 years before different forums, including Bar Council of India, Bombay HC and SC."Each of these parties has come to us complaining of a wrong, and each has been the author of a good part of it. Between them, they have occupied the time of the Bar Council, an HC and this court for 11 years. That time belonged to other litigants, waiting for relief they genuinely needed. We record our strong disapproval of the conduct of both. In view of the conduct of each party, we find it fit to impose costs," the bench said.The bench noted that the two litigants approached the court in the confident expectation of vindication."Every fact of consequence has had to be prised out of a record in which suppression, embellishment and afterthought are the common currency of both sides. The machinery of justice is not a facility placed at the disposal of parties to settle scores, to salvage reputations they have themselves imperilled, or to extract advantage from a controversy of their own making.We say at the outset, and give our reasons in what follows, that neither the appellant nor the respondent leaves this court with credit," it said."Record in these matters makes for compelling reading. Litigation of this kind holds a certain fascination, and we do not pretend otherwise. But a court is not an auditorium, and the drama of a case is no measure of its merit. Stripped of its theatre, what these proceedings disclose is a controversy which two litigants have between them manufactured, prolonged and brought to the highest court in the country, each in the hope that we would be sufficiently diverted by the spectacle to overlook their own part in creating it. We have not been," it said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court disapproves the practice of influential people indulging in "luxury litigation" It imposed a cost of Rs 5 lakh each on warring litigants for not approaching the court with "clean hands" A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta rejected the plea of actress Rehana Khan.

Article Title: Ex-diplomat Navdeep Suri flags 'trouble establishing citizenship' during Punjab SIR
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Former diplomat Navdeep Suri on Sunday said he was facing "trouble establishing his citizenship" during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Punjab, despite having represented India in three countries.In a post on X, Suri shared his experience with the voter roll revision and said he was asked to provide "unspecified documents" to establish that he was an Indian citizen."Sharing my experience with #SIR in Punjab. Went to BLO, submitted Voter ID and Aadhaar card, was assured that everything is in order. Got a message today from a volunteer saying some details don’t match with SIR in 2003!" Suri said.He said that after speaking to the booth-level officer (BLO), he was asked to collect a notice and return with documents proving his citizenship."Spoke with BLO, was told that I should come and collect the notice. And then come again with unspecified documents that show I am an Indian citizen. Replied that I was not in India in 2003, so they’ve asked for passport as proof," he added.Suri said he had documents apart from his voter ID and Aadhaar, but questioned what the process would mean for ordinary citizens."I happen to have documents other than voter ID and Aadhaar card.But can’t help asking: If I have trouble establishing my citizenship after representing India in three countries, what’s the fate of the common citizen? Ease of Living, I presume!" he said.Former ambassador Navdeep Suri has served as India's high commissioner to Australia and ambassador to UAE and Egypt.The SIR was first launched in Bihar in June 2025. Following the exercise, more than 60 lakh names, including those of deceased voters, were removed from the electoral rolls. In West Bengal, around 90 lakh voters were deleted from the rolls ahead of the assembly elections.Under the SIR process, voters who were not included in the 2002 or 2003 electoral rolls are required to submit documents linking them to people included in those legacy rolls. The Election Commission of India (ECI) had initially listed 11 acceptable documents, excluding Aadhaar.Following proceedings in the Supreme Court , the poll panel expanded the list to include Aadhaar as an acceptable document.The Supreme Court has also made observations on the broader constitutional implications of the exercise, stressing that while the ECI has the power to revise electoral rolls, those powers cannot be "untrammelled" and must comply with principles of transparency and natural justice.
Article Summary: Navdeep Suri has served as India's high commissioner to Australia and ambassador to UAE and Egypt. Suri shared his experience with the voter roll revision in Punjab. He said he was asked to provide "unspecified documents" to establish that he was an Indian citizen.

Hailee Steinfeld is discovering that motherhood can change the way a person sees even the most familiar parts of life. Just months after welcoming her daughter with Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen , the actress has opened up about a lesson that reaches far beyond parenting. For Steinfeld, becoming a mother has made self-love less personal and more powerful.Steinfeld shared the reflection on, in the summer edition of hernewsletter, where she answered questions from readers. One fan asked what her daughter had already taught her despite being so young. Steinfeld's answer offered a glimpse into how quickly motherhood had begun to reshape her thinking.“Where to start! One of the most unexpected things I’ve learned from my daughter is the importance of modeling unconditional self-love.”Steinfeld then explained that she was still figuring out how to put that lesson into practice. Her point, however, was clear. A child does not only learn from what a parent says. They also learn from what a parent believes about themselves.She wrote that, during the early stages of raising a daughter, she had realized that the way she sees herself can influence the way her daughter eventually sees herself.That idea gives her comment a deeper meaning. Steinfeld was not simply talking about confidence or feeling good about one's appearance.She was talking about the example a parent sets every day, including the way they respond to mistakes, pressure and their own insecurities.For someone who has spent much of her life in the public eye, the realization carries particular weight. Steinfeld grew up working in entertainment, where appearances and public judgment can become part of everyday life. Motherhood appears to have given her a different reason to think about those pressures.Steinfeld and Allen entered parenthood in April 2026. The couple announced the arrival of their baby girl through Steinfeld'snewsletter, describing themselves as grateful and blessed while asking fans to respect the intimacy of those early moments.By June, Steinfeld had begun sharing more reflections about the experience. She later revealed that her daughter's name is, in a June 19 letter dedicated to the baby. In that emotional message, she described her daughter as someone who had already taught her more than she expected to learn.The timing matters. Steinfeld's comments about self-love came only a few months into motherhood, when the experience was still new and unpredictable. She was not presenting herself as someone who had mastered parenting. Instead, she was acknowledging that she was learning alongside her daughter.That honesty is part of what makes the reflection resonate. New parents are often expected to have answers. Steinfeld's approach suggests something different: sometimes the most meaningful part of becoming a parent is realizing how much there is still to learn.Allen has also spoken openly about the impact of becoming a father. Before his daughter was born, the Bills quarterback said he was looking forward to becoming a dad and made it clear that the role meant more to him than any professional achievement.“Becoming a dad is something that I will take with great pride,” Allen said in January. “This is the most important thing I’ll be in my life, being a dad.”That perspective became even clearer after Harper's arrival.In April, Allen explained that his reasons for playing football had begun to change. The quarterback, who has spent years under the pressure of leading Buffalo, suggested that fatherhood had given his ambitions a more personal foundation. His football career remains important, but his motivation now extends beyond himself.Weeks later, Allen became visibly emotional while speaking about his daughter at a charity event supporting the Patricia Allen Fund. He said becoming a father had changed the way he viewed parents dealing with serious challenges involving their children.“Having my daughter,” Allen said, “I look at parents differently, because I can picture myself in that situation now where I never could.”The quarterback went on to describe the year as completely different and spoke about the instinct every parent can understand: wanting to protect a child from pain.His comments reveal a side of Allen that is easy to miss during the intensity of an NFL season. On the football field, his world is built around competition and results. Fatherhood has introduced something he cannot control and cannot solve with preparation.Steinfeld has also spoken about slowing down and appreciating the fleeting nature of having a newborn. During a June 17livestream, she said her goal was to be fully present and absorb as much of the experience as possible because children change so quickly.That mindset connects naturally with her comments about self-love.Motherhood is often portrayed as a story about what parents give up. Steinfeld's experience suggests it can also be about what they discover. Looking back at Tom Brady’s Tampa Bay Buccaneers years, some memories have little to do with championships or records. One came on Aug. 28, 2021, when Brady gave a young Buccaneers fan his jersey during Tampa Bay’s preseason finale against the Houston Texans. The boy reportedly started crying tears of joy, turning a simple exchange between an NFL star and a young supporter into one of the night’s most touching moments.The gesture stood out because Brady understood what it meant to be on the other side of that interaction. After the game, he explained that athletes can leave a lasting impression on people, especially children who look up to them. His words also showed why he felt connected to the moment.The story emerged during Tampa Bay’s preseason finale on August 28, 2021, at NRG Stadium in Houston. ESPN reporter Jenna Laine shared the moment during the broadcast, reporting that Brady had given a young fan in the stands his jersey and that the boy “started crying tears of joy.”Brady later addressed the interaction during his postgame press conference that same night. Rather than treat it as a passing moment, he connected it to his own childhood and the responsibility athletes have when young fans watch them.“I think we can all make an impact on our communities in a positive way,” Brady said during the August 28, 2021, postgame press conference. “It’s great to see the support of the fans come back out. I was a kid once, too.”That final sentence gave the gesture a deeper meaning. Brady had spent years as one of football’s biggest stars, but he still remembered being a child who watched professional athletes and admired what they represented. For the young Buccaneers fan, seeing Brady in person was already special. Receiving his jersey turned that experience into something personal.The moment also came during a preseason finale that gave Brady and the Buccaneers plenty to feel good about on the field. Tampa Bay defeated Houston 23-16, and Brady completed 11 of 14 passes for 154 yards and one touchdown. He started the game and helped the Buccaneers establish an early lead before head coach Bruce Arians pulled him and most of the first-team offense after three drives. The Buccaneers had planned to give their starters roughly a half of action, but Arians felt they had done enough.Brady’s best stretch came on Tampa Bay’s second offensive possession. After the Buccaneers opened with a false-start penalty and a three-and-out, Brady settled into the offense quickly. He completed seven straight passes on a 91-yard touchdown drive, including a 24-yard scoring connection with Chris Godwin.The performance gave Tampa Bay exactly what it wanted before the regular season. Brady got live snaps, worked with his starters and helped the defending Super Bowl champions finish the preseason with a victory. Yet the statistic that mattered most to one young fan had nothing to do with passing yards.It was the jersey.Brady’s career had already produced countless memorable moments by August 2021, including seven Super Bowl victories and a championship with Tampa Bay months earlier. Still, the exchange with that young supporter showed another side of his influence. He did not need a record or a trophy to make an impression that night.Five years later, the moment remains a reminder that an NFL superstar’s impact can reach beyond the field. Brady gave one young Buccaneers fan something tangible to take home, but his own explanation captured the bigger idea. Sometimes, the most meaningful memories in sports come from a simple gesture that tells a fan their hero noticed them.

Article Title: 'Does anyone actually care?': Sreejesh launches scathing attack after India’s World Cup exit
Article Text:

Two-time Olympic bronze medallist and former India goalkeeper P. R. Sreejesh has launched a scathing attack on the Indian hockey management after both the men’s and women’s teams failed to reach the semifinals of their respective World Cups.The men’s campaign ended on Monday with a 3-5 defeat against Argentina at the Wagener Hockey Stadium in Amstelveen, Netherlands. India will now play Belgium in the seventh-place classification match.India’s hopes of reaching the semifinals had already taken a major blow after a 1-3 defeat to co-hosts Netherlands on Saturday. Against Argentina, India needed a win to stay in contention but their defensive frailties and failure to convert chances proved costly.Argentina took the lead just 36 seconds into the contest when Joaquin Toscani punished an error by Jarmanpreet Singh, who failed to intercept a ball across the goalmouth. Nicolas della Torre doubled the advantage in the sixth minute, converting Argentina’s second penalty corner.Sukhjeet Singh gave India a lifeline in the 10th minute, but they were unable to capitalise on their chances in the second quarter. Tomas Domene restored Argentina’s two-goal cushion in the 33rd minute before completing his brace with a penalty stroke in the 45th.Lucas Toscani then made it 5-2.Sukhjeet scored again in the 58th minute and Hardil Singh reduced the deficit further a minute later, but India could not complete the comeback.India also wasted all seven of their penalty corners, once again exposing their struggles to convert opportunities. Despite enjoying possession, they failed to produce enough end product.Sreejesh, who retired after the Paris Olympics, took to X after India’s exits and questioned the approach and accountability within Indian hockey.“Don’t worry… the World Cup doesn’t matter.“The Asian Games are coming. Win a medal there, and then we can start dreaming about LA 2028. Apparently, that’s enough to cover everything that went wrong at the World Cup.“Women’s chief coach on holiday just before the World Cup — and the girls still fought their hearts out and exceeded expectations. Credit to the players. But where is the accountability? Do we really expect a team to perform at its best when the chief coach is away during the final phase of preparation?“Men’s team loses to a top team → ‘It’s a learning experience.’Beats an Asian team → ‘Great victory.’Plays good hockey → ‘Good performance.’“But here’s the uncomfortable question: Are we building a team to PLAY good hockey, or a team capable of WINNING against the best in the world?“Stop hiding behind ‘learning’, ‘good hockey’ and future tournaments. The World Cup is not a rehearsal. It is the World Cup.“So who is going to ask the difficult questions? Who is going to demand accountability? And most importantly… Does anyone actually care?”Sreejesh had previously questioned the quality of Indian coaching after his tenure as the junior men’s team coach was not renewed. He had guided the side to a bronze medal at last year’s Junior World Cup.The women’s team had also missed out on a semifinal place after being held to a goalless draw by Australia in their final second-round match on Sunday. The result sent Australia through to the last four on the basis of having scored more goals.With both Indian teams failing to reach the semifinals, Sreejesh’s comments have added to the scrutiny over India’s ability to consistently compete with the world’s leading hockey nations.

Article Title: What the Steelers' Aaron Rodgers insurance policy actually means for their 2026 season
Article Text:
Aaron Rodgers (Getty Images)

Will the Steelers actually keep four quarterbacks on their 53-man roster?

What happens to the Steelers after Aaron Rodgers' final season?

The Pittsburgh Steelers are heading into 2026 with Aaron Rodgers at quarterback, Mike McCarthy calling the shots and genuine Super Bowl expectations sitting on their shoulders. Rodgers is back for one final year, the offensive line is improved, and the AFC North title from last season gives them real momentum. But Pittsburgh isn't just hoping Rodgers stays healthy and plays well. They are quietly building one of the more unusual depth charts at quarterback the league has seen, and it tells you a lot about how they see this season playing out.That appears to be where things are heading. ESPN's Todd Archer released a roster projection Monday that has Pittsburgh keeping all four of their quarterbacks: Aaron Rodgers, Mason Rudolph, Will Howard and Drew Allar. All four. On one roster.Archer acknowledges it breaks convention. McCarthy has never carried four quarterbacks on his opening 53-man roster. But Archer argues this season is different, writing that the "toughest decision facing the Steelers comes behind Aaron Rodgers and the deliberation between keeping two or three backup quarterbacks."The reasoning makes sense when you look at it clearly. Rudolph is the obvious emergency option, a veteran who knows the system.Howard and Allar are young and raw, but their preseason work has been encouraging. Archer notes that the two young quarterbacks are "progressing well under coach Mike McCarthy and could handle filling in for Rodgers in case of emergency." The gap between Rudolph and that younger pair is significant enough that cutting any of them would be a gamble Pittsburgh doesn't need to take right now.So yes, four quarterbacks. It is unusual. It is also, given the circumstances, probably the right call.That question is already being asked, and it matters more than most fans want to admit. ESPN's Dan Graziano addressed it directly in a quarterback outlook piece Thursday, laying out what this season really means for Pittsburgh beyond just wins and losses.McCarthy gets a full year to evaluate Howard and Allar up close. If Rodgers performs well and Pittsburgh goes deep, the transition happens on Pittsburgh's terms. Graziano sees that as the most likely outcome, writing that "Rodgers rides off into the sunset and the Steelers are left to evaluate Allar, Howard and potential 2027 draft picks as their long-term solution."But if Aaron Rodgers struggles, the decision gets made for them. Allar's strong showing in the first preseason game already has people paying attention. Pittsburgh would not hesitate to turn to him if the situation demanded it.Either way, this season ends with the Steelers at a crossroads. Four quarterbacks on the roster isn't just depth planning. It's the organization keeping every option open before a decision that will define the next several years.
Article Summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have four quarterbacks on their 53-man roster. Aaron Rodgers, Mason Rudolph, Will Howard and Drew Allar are all on one roster. ESPN's Todd Archer says it's unusual, but probably the right call. If Rodgers performs well and Pittsburgh goes deep, the transition happens on Pittsburgh's terms.

San Francisco 49ers owner and CEO Jed York was arrested in Ohio on Sunday after police accused him of trying to arrange a sexual encounter for $140. The case moved quickly, with York pleading no contest to amended misdemeanor charges on Monday. He was sentenced to one day in jail, received credit for time already served and was ordered to pay a $1,150 fine. The Cleveland Browns made their quarterback decision on August 24, 2026, and Mina Kimes had plenty to say about it. Todd Monken named Deshaun Watson the starter over Shedeur Sanders after a close competition. The choice came just two days after Watson was booed during Cleveland’s 31-7 preseason loss to Buffalo. Kimes argued that the reaction was not simply about Watson’s past. She believes his uneven play has also given Browns fans reason to turn on him.Watson’s return already carries plenty of pressure. He missed the entire 2025 season after an Achilles injury and has struggled to stay healthy since joining Cleveland. Now, he will open the 2026 regular season as QB1. Kimes believes the Browns have once again chosen to stand firmly behind him, even as their relationship with the fanbase continues to get more complicated.Recently, Mina Kimes shared her reaction in a video posted to Bluesky . Her main argument was simple: Watson cannot dismiss the boos as purely personal when his play has also failed to win supporters back.“I think Watson is wrong,” Kimes said. “I don’t think he’s being booed for personal reasons. Maybe by some! There’s definitely fans who never got over it. But I think he’s being booed because he’s been bad at football.”The frustration became especially clear during the Bills game on August 22. Watson completed just 5 of 12 passes for 67 yards and threw an interception. Cleveland lost 31-7, and the home crowd booed Watson during his appearance.That came after Watson addressed the possibility of being booed before the game. Recently, he said, “I don’t care.” After the loss, however, his tone changed. The NFL suspended him for 11 games in 2022 for violating its personal conduct policy. Kimes argued that Cleveland has not demanded enough accountability from its quarterback.The Browns, however, say the decision was about football. Monken evaluated Watson and Sanders throughout training camp, preseason games and joint practices before making his call. He said Watson gives Cleveland its “best chance” to win and move the offense.The numbers show why the decision remains debatable. Through two preseason appearances, Watson completed 16 of 27 passes for 162 yards with one interception. Sanders completed 15 of 22 passes for 153 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions.Still, Monken made his choice. Watson will start the September 13 opener against Jacksonville, followed by a road game against Tampa Bay. Former Pakistan captain Salman Butt has hit back at the British media after sections of the UK press branded the current Pakistan side the “worst team in 50 years” following their heavy defeat to England in the first Test at Headingley.Butt defended Pakistan’s players and questioned the tone of the criticism, arguing that the team had never claimed to be a dominant force in world cricket. He also took aim at England’s squad composition while making a pointed comparison between the two teams.“We never said we were world champions. We never claimed to be a big team, nor did we boast about ourselves,” Butt stated. “What do you think of yourself? What kind of things do you say? Phases come in teams. Teams might not play well.”Butt then turned his attention to England’s history of players from different countries representing the national side. He argued that Pakistan, regardless of its current struggles, fields a team developed within its own cricket system.“At least no matter how our team is, even if it's the worst ever, it's our own,” Butt declared. “It's not from a Commonwealth, with the captain from Ireland, the wicket-keeper from South Africa...one guy from Scotland, one guy Australian, and one guy from the West Indies. This isn't six nations playing as a team.”His comments came after Pakistan were comprehensively outplayed by England in the opening Test of the three-match series. Article Title: 'State tried to airbrush Imran khan out of existence': Atherton on appeal for former Pakistan PM

Former England captain Michael Atherton has revealed why he joined a group of 21 former international cricketers in calling on Pakistani authorities to ensure imprisoned former Pakistan captain and Prime Minister Imran Khan receives proper medical treatment.Imran has been in prison since 2023 after being convicted in corruption cases, charges he has vehemently denied. Concerns over his health have grown in recent months, with reports earlier this year claiming that he had lost sight in one eye.The reports prompted former cricketers to appeal to the authorities for his medical care. Last week, 21 former international players again wrote to the authorities after Imran was reportedly taken to a hospital following an order from the country’s top court, but was allegedly not properly examined.Atherton, speaking on a Sky Sports cricket podcast alongside former England captain Nasser Hussain, said the appeal was not simply about ensuring medical treatment for Imran. He also expressed concern over what he described as an attempt to erase the former Pakistan leader from public life.“Nass [Nasser Hussain] and I were among 21 former captains who sent a second letter yesterday, a humanitarian appeal for Imran Khan to get the requisite level of treatment.But I suppose the basic theme was the way the state has tried to airbrush Imran almost out of existence, which is increasingly difficult to do in a social media age,” Atherton said on a Sky Sports cricket podcast in the company of Hussain.The group included several prominent former cricketers from across the cricketing world. Former India captains Kapil Dev, Sunil Gavaskar and Dilip Vengsarkar were also among those who signed the appeal.The involvement of the three Indian cricketers was particularly notable given the political tensions between India and Pakistan and Imran’s own history as Pakistan’s prime minister.Kapil explained why he felt compelled to support his former cricketing rival and friend, while also acknowledging that Pakistani cricketers could be in a difficult position if they spoke publicly.“I don’t blame Pakistani cricketers for not speaking up. They have to live there. But I would like to support my friend, whom we admired and played with," Kapil said.The former India captain stressed that the appeal was not about intervening in Pakistan’s legal process but about ensuring basic care and dignity for a prisoner.“We don't know the law of the country, that's fine. But humility and simple facilities should be given to a prisoner, whoever he may be. And he was a former prime minister of the country and a top cricketer.“We want him to get the best treatment, [that's] what we are asking for. We are not asking for anything else, we are not asking for any replies, we are requesting," the former India captain added.Imran led Pakistan to their only men’s ODI World Cup title in 1992 and was considered one of the finest all-rounders the game has ever seen, before moving into politics and eventually becoming the country’s prime minister. His imprisonment has continued to draw international attention, while concerns over his health have added another dimension to the controversy surrounding his detention.

Imran has been in prison since 2023 after being convicted in corruption cases. Concerns over his health have grown in recent months, with reports earlier this year claiming that he had lost sight in one eye.

How did Serena Williams almost die after giving birth to Alexis Olympia Ohanian Jr.

How did Alexis Ohanian support Serena Williams during her recovery

Why did Serena Williams choose family when she stepped away from tennis

Serena Williams’ story of motherhood is also a story of survival. In 2017, the tennis star won the Australian Open while eight weeks pregnant, then nearly died after giving birth to her daughter, Alexis Olympia Ohanian Jr. An emergency C-section was followed by a pulmonary embolism, more surgery and six weeks in bed. Serena later returned to the highest level of tennis, reaching four straight Grand Slam finals. Her daughter Olympia became an important part of that journey. Years later, Serena chose to step away from singles tennis to focus on her family, while continuing to build her life beyond the court.Serena’s pregnancy had gone well, but the birth of Olympia on September 1, 2017, quickly became dangerous. Olympia was delivered by emergency C-section after her heart rate dropped sharply during contractions. The surgery itself went well, and Serena was able to hold her daughter. The serious problems started about a day later.Serena suddenly had trouble breathing. Because she had a history of blood clots, she suspected she was having another pulmonary embolism, a condition in which a blood clot blocks blood flow in the lungs.She asked for a CT scan and blood thinner treatment. Doctors later found several small clots in her lungs.The treatment then caused another problem. Serena’s intense coughing made her C-section wound open. Doctors found a large hematoma, or a collection of blood, in her abdomen. She needed more surgery and another procedure to help stop future clots from reaching her lungs. After leaving the hospital, Serena spent the first six weeks of motherhood in bed and had difficulty even walking.Serena later described the experience in a CNN opinion piece, making clear just how close she believed she had come to losing her life.“I almost died after giving birth to my daughter, Olympia. Yet I consider myself fortunate… When I finally made it home to my family, with only days left in my recovery, I felt a deep sense of gratitude just to hold my baby girl in my arms.”The CNN piece was also about the wider problem of maternal health and the need for better access to care. Serena credited the doctors and nurses who treated her with helping save her life.For Serena, recovering from childbirth was not only about getting her body strong enough to play tennis again. She was also learning how to care for a newborn while she was unable to move normally.Her husband, Alexis Ohanian, was there during that difficult period. In Serena’s 2018 Vogue interview, Ohanian spoke about how hard it was to watch his wife struggle while he could not take away what she was going through. Serena also described how difficult those first weeks were as a new mother.That made her return to tennis different from any comeback she had made before. She was not simply trying to get her ranking back. She was trying to find a way to be a professional athlete and a mother at the same time.When Serena returned to competition, she faced another challenge. After her long break, she had fallen far down the rankings and had to work her way back into major events. She eventually reached the 2018 Wimbledon final, less than a year after giving birth.Olympia was born into a world where her mother was already one of the biggest names in tennis. But after the difficult birth, motherhood gave Serena a different reason to keep going.During her return, Serena spoke openly about the emotional side of being a mother and an athlete. Her run to the Wimbledon final in 2018 became one of the clearest signs that she could still compete at the highest level after everything her body had gone through.After the Wimbledon final, Serena also dedicated her performance to mothers watching her. She had lost to Angelique Kerber, but the result did not take away from what she had achieved by reaching the final so soon after giving birth.“Olympia, does mama look good out here? You’re the reason I’m here, you’re my motivation. To all the moms out there, I was playing for you today. It’s okay to have hard days, but we keep fighting.”That message summed up what her comeback had come to mean. Serena was not hiding the difficult parts of motherhood. She was showing that returning to work after having a child can involve fear, setbacks and days when the body simply does not cooperate.Her run did not stop at Wimbledon. Serena reached four straight Grand Slam singles finals after becoming a mother: Wimbledon and the US Open in 2018, followed by the Australian Open and Wimbledon in 2019. She did not win those finals, but reaching them showed how quickly she had returned to the top of the sport.By 2022, Serena was ready for another major change. She did not want to call it retirement. In her Vogue essay announcing her decision to move away from professional tennis, she called it an “evolution.”Her decision was closely tied to her family. Serena wrote about Olympia’s wish to become a big sister and her own desire to have another child. At the same time, she wanted to give more attention to Serena Ventures and the other parts of her life that had grown alongside her tennis career.“I have never liked the word retirement… Maybe the best word to describe what I’m up to is evolution. I’m here to tell you that I’m evolving away from tennis, toward other things that are important to me… My daughter wants to be a big sister, and I want to be there for my family.”Vogue published Serena’s essay in August 2022, ahead of what she described as her final US Open. She later welcomed her second daughter, Adira River Ohanian, with Alexis Ohanian in August 2023.Serena’s tennis story has since taken another unexpected turn. In 2026, she returned to competitive tennis, making her comeback first in doubles and later joining Carlos Alcaraz for the US Open mixed doubles event. That means her relationship with the sport is still evolving, even after she stepped away from singles competition in 2022.Her motherhood journey remains one of the most personal parts of that story. Serena went from a frightening medical crisis after Olympia’s birth to competing in Grand Slam finals again. She then made a choice to put family at the centre of her next chapter. For Serena, strength was not only about winning another match. It was also about surviving, recovering and finding a new reason to keep moving forward.
Article Summary: Serena Williams almost died after giving birth to her daughter, Alexis Olympia Ohanian Jr. An emergency C-section was followed by a pulmonary embolism, more surgery and six weeks in bed. Serena later returned to the highest level of tennis, reaching four straight Grand Slam finals.

Article Title: "I’ve sacrificed a lot": Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders' director Kelli Finglass confronts the possibility of walking away from the America's Sweetheart
Article Text:
America’s Sweethearts

Kelli Finglass on Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders and social media criticism

Kelli Finglass reveals her future with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders

For Kelli Finglass , leading the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders has never been only about flawless routines and game-day glamour. Her role has placed her at the center of auditions, tough decisions, television scrutiny and the changing pressures faced by young performers. As Netflix’sreturns for season three, Finglass is reflecting on criticism, motherhood, vulnerability and the possibility of eventually stepping away.Finglass knows exactly what it takes to become a Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader because she once stood where the dancers now stand. She performed for the Cowboys from 1984 to 1989 before taking over as coach in 1991. Her career has since become closely tied to the evolution of the organization on television.The Netflix series has brought unprecedented attention to the cheerleaders, but that visibility has a downside. Social media criticism can follow the women beyond the dance studio, something Finglass says she has seen affect members of the team.She does not make a habit of reading online comments herself. Still, she understands the emotional weight they can carry.“The words of people, while they can be very, very uplifting...Like in my personal case with my skin cancer journey, the people that reached out to me were extremely supportive," she said in an interview with Vanity Fair."Words can hurt and they can also heal. I’m trusting humanity to help figure this one out because it’s a much bigger thing than I can solve. But the girls being busy and focused and supportive of each other is where our strength will remain.”That outlook reflects a major lesson Finglass has learned through years of television. The cheerleaders do not need to appear perfect all the time.Finglass has also reconsidered what leadership means as she has grown older. She says motherhood changed how she sees the young women she coaches and helped her understand the struggles they face away from performances.Her approach has shifted from demanding perfection toward encouraging honesty and resilience.“I spent practically my whole career trying to create flawless performances, and what we’ve learned through TV is that vulnerability is actually more attractive. People love when they can relate to somebody, and that’s been an unexpected “aha” for me—for these girls to not project perfection, but rather be honest about their victories and honest about their struggles, has, I hope, given viewers something to find hope in and find something they can relate to.Now entering her 35th season with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, retirement is no longer an impossible thought. Finglass says her family could ultimately influence that decision, especially as she looks toward becoming a grandmother someday.“I have, but we’re so busy, we don’t have time to think about anything except the next hour. It would be a personal decision. I’ve sacrificed a lot of time with my family. My daughter is married, my son is in a relationship, and when I ever get the honor to be a grandma…I want that time if and when I have grandchildren. That would definitely give me a heartfelt reason to go to a new chapter.”For now, Finglass remains focused on the next generation. Her story has become intertwined with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, but her lasting message may be simpler: perfection is impressive, while vulnerability can be powerful.
Article Summary: Kelli Finglass is reflecting on criticism, motherhood, vulnerability and the possibility of eventually stepping away. She performed for the Cowboys from 1984 to 1989 before taking over as coach in 1991. Her approach has shifted from demanding perfection toward encouraging honesty and resilience.

Article Title: What happened to Alyshia Rushing? Mama A’s Alabama car crash death leaves four children, fans ‘heartbroken’

TikTok creator Alyshia Rushing, known online as “Mama A,” died at 26 after a two-vehicle crash in Montgomery, Alabama, on Saturday, August 22. A GoFundMe fundraiser has since been launched to help the children and their father with their needs after her death. Rushing had built a large TikTok following by sharing videos about motherhood and everyday family life. Her sudden death has left many followers grieving.The crash happened around 2:15 a.m. Saturday in Montgomery, between Taylor Road and Chantilly Parkway. WSFA reported that police found Alyshia Rushing at the scene with life-threatening injuries. She was later pronounced dead.The crash involved two vehicles. The driver of the other vehicle, 20-year-old Landon Dunn, also died at the scene. An unidentified passenger who was traveling with Rushing was taken to a hospital for treatment. Police are investigating what caused the crash, and no cause has been released so far.Rushing was known to her TikTok followers as “Mama A.” Her account had more than 470,000 followers, with much of her content focused on life as a mother. Her four children were a major part of the content she shared online.Fans quickly began sharing messages after news of her death spread. One wrote, “One of my favorite TikTok content creators passed away and I just watched her videos a few days ago. RIP to Alyshia Rushing. Lord please protect her babies.”Another follower said, “Alyshia Rushing was my favorite content creators frfr. Watch her every night in bed! Seeing her videos now and knowing she’s gone and left behind 4 kids is truly heartbreaking! Like I’m really taken aback.”A third fan wrote, “RIP to Alyshia Rushing. So sad & unfortunate, she was really getting herself back together & flourishing. I really hope one day her children finds all her videos and sees how much she loved and cared for them.”A GoFundMe titled “In Loving Memory of Alyshia ‘Mama A’ Rushing” has been created for Karter, Raelynn, Zoey and Aydan. The fundraiser says Alyshia was “their mother, caregiver, provider, safe place, and greatest source of love.”It adds that their father is now responsible for caring for all four children. The fundraiser is meant to help with food, clothing, housing, school expenses, transportation, childcare, activities and counseling. It also says the money will help the father “prepare for future expenses” so the children “can continue growing, learning, and healing in a safe and supportive environment.”The organizers also warned that other GoFundMe pages may appear and said this is “the only fundraiser authorized to support Alyshia’s children and their father.”Many followers are now looking back at Rushing’s videos as they mourn a creator they had followed through her family-focused content.
Article Summary: Alyshia Rushing, 26, died after a two-vehicle crash in Montgomery, Alabama. Rushing was found with life-threatening injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene. She leaves behind four children: Karter, Raelynn, Zoey and Aydan. A GoFundMe has been launched to help the children and their father.

Article Title: “They ejected a woman?” Enes Kanter Freedom’s controversy extended as fans question ex NBA star’s removal from Fever-Sky game

Fans react to Enes Kanter Freedom's ejection

Enes Kanter Freedom was pulled out of Wintrust Arena during the third quarter of Sunday's Fever-Sky game, and the fallout has outlasted the final buzzer by days. Security walked him off the baseline to a wall of boos after a heated back and forth with Sky guard Natasha Cloud, and within minutes he was telling his side of the story online.What happened in that stretch of the third quarter is still getting pieced together from competing accounts. Fans who watched it unfold from courtside disagree on who started it, and Freedom's own explanation has only added more layers to a night that briefly overshadowed a dominant Fever win.Enes Kanter Freedom, an 11-year NBA veteran who last played in the league in 2022, was seated courtside wearing a shirt reading "Woman noun. Adult human female." Cloud scored a basket late in the third quarter and appeared to direct comments his way from the floor. Freedom stood, put his hands up, and within moments arena security had moved in and walked him out while both Fever and Sky fans booed.Fan Trista Smith, who said she was sitting next to him, backed his version of events. "She came and got in his face, so he stood up," Smith told reporters, adding that she didn't know Freedom before that night and didn't think the ejection was fair.Sky forward Azurá Stevens kept her postgame comments brief. "There was just a fan incident, security handled it," she said, before turning the conversation back to the game.Coach Tyler Marsh said Cloud didn't want to become a distraction and that the team told her otherwise. "We all embrace her as someone that protects our team," Marsh said, adding that Cloud has the Sky's full support. Fever guard Caitlin Clark said she missed the whole thing. "I didn't see it," she said, noting her focus was on the huddle. Fever coach Stephanie White downplayed the incident afterward, calling it a distraction from a franchise-record 18 three-pointers and Clark's own career high. "It's a social media thing," she said.Freedom didn't wait long to respond. "I just got kicked out of a WNBA game for supporting WOMEN!" he posted, framing the removal as retaliation for his stance rather than anything he did on the baseline. In a separate post, the ex NBA star added, “It’s always women hating on other women.”He'd already stirred things up before tipoff, sharing a video of a confrontation with protesters outside the arena and posting from a restroom line during halftime referencing WNBA "rules."The league's collective bargaining agreement states that only women are eligible to play, though it doesn't define gender identity directly, and Freedom has said he intends to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft. The league has not said whether the incident will carry any further consequences.Social media picked the story up fast, and reactions split in almost every direction. Some mocked the situation, some defended Freedom, and others used it to take shots at the league itself.Colin (@BasedCLC): "They ejected a woman?"Daniel (@golfandstufff): "Looks like they could use "her" help…. Busy arguing with the crowd and not playing ball…"bbowden18 (@Bluestown901): "LET HER PLAY!"Will Van Booraem (@WillVanBooraem): "Kicking out the projected #1 overall pick in the 2027 WNBA draft is crazy"Kaneki (@Sadboy0801): "She wanted her voice heard 😭😂😂"NQ OWNER (@nqowner): "Yapping at the audience while being down by 6 is crazy work🤣🤣🤣"Most of the replies leaned into the joke rather than the politics behind it, though a handful used the moment to criticize the league's handling of the incident entirely.

Can Nico Daws beat Jake Allen and David Rittich for the Devils’ No. 1 goalie spot?

The New Jersey Devils will enter the 2026-27 season without a clear No. 1 goaltender, but Hall-of-Fame goalie Martin Brodeur believes Nico Daws deserves a real chance to take the job. After moving Jacob Markstrom to the Florida Panthers, New Jersey has left the door open for a new starter to emerge.Jake Allen and David Rittich are also in the mix, but Daws could have the biggest opportunity of his young NHL career. Brodeur, who serves as the Devils’ executive vice president of hockey operations, believes the 25-year-old deserves an opportunity to show what he can do in the NHL.According to Brodeur, the Devils are comfortable letting their goaltenders compete for the starting job rather than naming a clear No. 1 before the season begins. “The best starter is going to get the net,” Brodeur told The Hockey News. “I don't think there's a clear-cut No. 1 goalie in net.”That gives Daws a real opening. The 2020 third-round pick has spent much of his career moving between the NHL and AHL, and Brodeur believes the Devils have not given him enough chances to show what he can do.“Nico Daws is a kid who needs a chance,” Brodeur said. “We've been developing him for four years.We didn't put great teams in front of him in Utica and obviously his development slowed down because of that. But we need to give him a chance to see what we have.”While Daws has limited NHL experience, he has already delivered one performance that stands out. In the Stadium Series game against the Philadelphia Flyers at MetLife Stadium, he stopped 51 shots. Brodeur still remembers that performance when discussing Daws’ potential.“We put him into the Stadium Series game at MetLife Stadium in front of 70,000 people and he had 51 saves against the Flyers. He's got it, I really believe in him, we just never gave him a chance,” Brodeur said.That belief could be important for Daws as he competes with Allen and Rittich. Allen brings much more NHL experience, while Rittich has also spent years in the league. But neither has been locked into a heavy workload in recent seasons.Brodeur acknowledged that Markstrom will be missed but believes the current group can give New Jersey what it needs.“Jake showed us a lot last year when he had to play. He played some solid minutes for us,” Brodeur said. “We feel that both goalies are able to play.”If Daws can make the most of his opportunity, he could quickly move from an inexperienced option to the Devils’ top goalie. Brodeur has made his belief clear. Now Daws has the chance to prove it on the ice.

Article Title: Inspiring story on motherhood by Naomi Osaka: “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter”- Tennis star reveals how self-care changed her approach to parenting
Article Text:
Inspiring story on motherhood by Naomi Osaka: “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter”- Tennis star reveals how self-care changed her approach to parenting

What did Naomi Osaka mean when she said self-care is part of motherhood ?

How did becoming a mother change Naomi Osaka’s view of tennis?

Why are boundaries so important to Osaka as a mother?

What can mothers learn from Naomi Osaka’s mental-health journey?

For Naomi Osaka, becoming a mother did not mean putting her own needs aside. Instead, it changed the way she thinks about self-care, mental health and life. The four-time Grand Slam champion, who has been open about her struggles with anxiety and pressure, has shared a simple but powerful message: “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter. ” Her words show why looking after yourself can also be an important part of being a good mother.Osaka became a mother in July 2023 when she welcomed her daughter, Shai, with rapper Cordae. Her journey into motherhood came during a major change in her life. She had stepped away from tennis for more than a year and was also trying to understand what she wanted from her career and her life.For Osaka, self-care is not about putting herself before her daughter. It is about making sure she is in a good place so she can also be there for her child.In her conversations about motherhood and mental health, Osaka has spoken about setting boundaries, taking time for herself and paying attention to what she needs. That can mean taking a quiet moment, meditating, getting enough rest when possible or simply saying no when something feels like too much.Her message also pushes back against the idea that mothers must always put themselves last.Being a mother does not mean a woman has to ignore her own feelings, needs or identity.Osaka’s approach is simple. A mother can love her child deeply and still need time for herself. In fact, taking care of her own mental and emotional health can help her be more present for her child.Tennis had been a huge part of Osaka’s life for years. She became world No. 1 and won four Grand Slam singles titles, including the US Open in 2018 and the Australian Open in 2019, 2021 and 2022.But success also came with pressure. Osaka made headlines in 2021 when she withdrew from the French Open after explaining that media duties were affecting her mental health. She later stepped away from tennis for an extended period.Becoming a mother gave her another chance to look at her life from a different point of view.Osaka returned to professional tennis in January 2024 after giving birth. The comeback was not easy. She had to rebuild her body, return to the demands of professional sport and deal with the normal ups and downs of competition.But motherhood also helped her understand that tennis was only one part of who she was.Winning was still important to her, but it was no longer the only thing that defined her. She could be a tennis player, a mother and her own person at the same time.That change in thinking also helped Osaka become more open about her emotions. Instead of feeling that she always had to appear strong, she became more comfortable talking about difficult moments and asking for support.Osaka has spent much of her career in the public eye. Her matches, interviews and personal life have all received huge attention. That level of attention can be difficult for anyone, and motherhood has given her even more reason to protect her private life and mental space.She has spoken about how hard it once was for her to say no because she worried about disappointing people. Over time, she learned that she could not make everyone happy and did not have to accept every demand placed on her.That lesson became an important part of how she approaches motherhood.For Osaka, boundaries can mean choosing when to work, taking time away from social media, protecting family time or simply refusing to take on something that could leave her overwhelmed.These choices are not about shutting people out. They are about knowing when she needs to step back.Her experience also sends an important message to other mothers. Saying no does not mean you care less. Taking a break does not mean you are lazy. Asking someone for help does not mean you have failed.Sometimes, protecting your own peace is what allows you to give more of yourself to the people you love.Perhaps the biggest lesson from Osaka’s story is that mental health should not be treated as something people have to hide.She has spoken openly about anxiety, pressure and the challenges that came with being a top athlete. She has also talked about wanting her daughter to grow up in an environment where talking about feelings is normal.Osaka has encouraged the idea that children should be able to express themselves, ask for help and understand their emotions. She has also talked about simple habits such as meditation, quiet time and spending meaningful time with family.For her, these lessons are not only things she can tell her daughter. They are things she can show her through her own actions.When a mother rests when she needs to, she shows her child that rest is important. When she talks about her feelings, she shows that emotions are normal. When she asks for help, she teaches her child that nobody has to deal with everything alone.That may be one of the most important parts of Osaka’s message.Motherhood does not have to mean losing yourself. A woman can still have dreams, a career, friendships, personal goals and time for herself while being a loving and devoted mother.Osaka’s journey shows that self-care is not about choosing yourself instead of your child. It is about making sure you are also cared for.For the tennis star, that balance has become part of the mother she wants to be. Her words, “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter,” capture that idea in the simplest way. Taking care of yourself is not taking love away from your child. Sometimes, it is what helps you give that love with more patience, energy and presence.
Article Summary: Tennis star Naomi Osaka reveals how self-care changed her approach to parenting. Osaka became a mother in July 2023 when she welcomed her daughter, Shai. The four-time Grand Slam champion has been open about her struggles with anxiety and pressure.
